text:
The Maple Leafs have lost seven straight, and Auston Matthews put it plainly, as The Leafs Nation reported: "it's on ourselves." The homestand that ended with a 1-0 loss to Edmonton was called the worst in the franchise's 109-year history by the same outlet. Toronto has one win in its last ten.

Matthews isn't the problem. He has 30 points in 23 games, and Toronto has taken 56% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 15 points better than without him. His own expected goals (11.4) are right in line with his 12 goals. If anything our numbers say the Leafs have been a little lucky with him on the ice (7.4 goals more than the chances deserve), which makes the losing even more pointed: the trouble is everywhere else.

Evolving-Hockey's notes from last season fit: his competition rated in the 99th percentile while his teammates ranked in the bottom 6%. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.0 chances per 60 from the home-plate area, 97th percentile. He's producing. The skid is a roster story, and the captain is saying so.
headline: Matthews is playing well on a team that isn't
